title: Cyrus and the Hymn
premise: Sebastian Okafor, a late-night radio host, begins taking calls from listeners who died the week before—each one asking them to pass on a message to someone still living, and each message a lie designed to open a door. The dead caller, a hymn-singing entity called the Choirmaster, was invited in generations ago by Sebastian's great-grandmother as payment for the family's uncanny gift for voices, and it has finally come to collect. As mirrors lag a second behind reality and the house seals itself against dawn, Sebastian must choose between broadcasting the final hymn that would bind the Choirmaster to their bloodline forever, or burning the family archive and losing their voice—literally—forever. In the end, Sebastian sings the hymn backwards on air, unmaking the pact but going mute, and finds that the people who love them learned to listen in other ways.
about_author: Zephyrine Whitlock is the pen name of a former overnight radio producer who spent seven years monitoring the 2 a.m. call-in lines and swears half the callers sounded pre-recorded. They write horror from a farmhouse with all the mirrors covered, purely as a precaution.

chapters.title: Dead Air
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Introduces the overnight show 'The Hour of the Wolf' and Sebastian's cheerful materialism about death. A caller named Marisol requests a song for her own funeral; Sebastian laughs it off. Beat: wry confidence before the fall.

chapters.title: The Second Voice
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Marisol's sister calls the station confirming Marisol died six days ago. Sebastian assumes a prank, but the call recording plays back with a second voice breathing underneath. Beat: first crack in disbelief.

chapters.title: Lag
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV, at their inherited family house. They notice their reflection in the hallway mirror finishes blinking a full second after they do. They blame exhaustion. Beat: creeping wrongness domesticated.

chapters.title: Inheritance of Static
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Exploring the house they never wanted—left by great-grandmother Adaeze Okafor, a famous gospel singer—they find a locked music room and a wall of reel-to-reel tapes labeled with dates spanning a century. Beat: the past asserting itself.

chapters.title: Caller Number Nine
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. On air, a dead caller gives a message for a living widow; when delivered, the widow weeps with gratitude—and then her phone goes permanently dead, and so does she, three days later. Beat: dread with a body count.

chapters.title: The Hymn
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. A caller hums four notes and asks Sebastian to 'pass it along.' The hum lodges in Sebastian's head, replaying involuntarily. Their cat refuses to enter the house. Beat: contamination.

chapters.title: Nkiru
chapters.summary: POV shift to Nkiru Adichie, an archivist and Sebastian's estranged ex, who receives Sebastian's panicked 4 a.m. voicemail and hears the hymn bleeding through the background. She recognizes the melody from her research. Beat: love re-entering through duty.

chapters.title: Adaeze's Bargain
chapters.summary: Nkiru's POV, in the city archives. She uncovers a 1923 contract: Adaeze Okafor traded her voice's 'shadow' to something called the Choirmaster for a voice that could make anyone believe anything—including, later, Sebastian's gift for radio. Beat: the inheritance revealed as a debt.

chapters.title: Every Mirror in the House
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. All mirrors now reflect one second late, and in that second, the reflections do things Sebastian isn't doing—smiling, mouthing words. Sebastian covers them with sheets. Beat: the house turning hostile.

chapters.title: The Choirmaster Speaks
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. On air, dead callers speak in unison, introducing themselves as one voice: the Choirmaster. It thanks Sebastian for 'keeping the door warm' and promises to collect at sunrise. Beat: the antagonist named.

chapters.title: What Was Invited In
chapters.summary: Nkiru's POV. She arrives at the house against Sebastian's protests. Together they find Adaeze's journal: the pact renews each generation, and the current holder—Sebastian—must either sing the final hymn at dawn or the Choirmaster takes the whole line. Beat: stakes crystallize.

chapters.title: Rules of the House
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. From the journal, they learn the rules: the Choirmaster can't enter rooms where its name isn't spoken, can't cross salt, and can't be seen directly without claiming the viewer's voice. Sebastian tests each rule; each fails in a new way. Beat: false safety.

chapters.title: The Living Callers
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV on air. Living listeners start calling in, entranced, humming the hymn across the city. The Choirmaster is using Sebastian's show as its throat. Sebastian cuts the broadcast; the transmitter keeps broadcasting without power. Beat: loss of control.

chapters.title: Nkiru's Research
chapters.summary: Nkiru's POV. She finds one documented case: in 1954, Sebastian's grandfather stalled the Choirmaster until dawn by singing counter-melodies, buying the family thirty years. The counter-melody notation is torn from the journal. Beat: hope with a hole in it.

chapters.title: The Missing Page
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. They tear the house apart for the missing page and find it hidden in the lining of Adaeze's performance gown—but the page is blank except when held up to a lagging mirror, where ink blooms one second behind. Beat: using the curse as a tool.

chapters.title: The Reflected Choir
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. In the mirror, Sebastian sees the reflection world fully populated: every Okafor who ever died, standing in rows, mouths open, waiting. One reflection—Adaeze—breaks formation and presses a warning to the glass. Beat: terror and kinship entwined.

chapters.title: Adaeze's Warning
chapters.summary: POV alternates. Through mirror-writing, Adaeze communicates: the hymn isn't a binding, it's a harvest. Singing it hands the Choirmaster every voice in the family line, living and dead. The counter-melody exists but requires 'a voice given freely to silence.' Beat: the trap defined.

chapters.title: Sunrise Is a Lie
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Dawn comes and goes; the sun rises outside but the house stays in night. The Choirmaster, on the phone lines, laughs: 'Sunrise is when I say it is.' Time inside the house has detached. Beat: the clock becomes the enemy.

chapters.title: The Neighbors
chapters.summary: Nkiru's POV. She tries to fetch help; the street outside loops, returning her to the front door no matter which direction she walks. A neighbor smiles with too many teeth and hums. Beat: the siege confirmed.

chapters.title: Sebastian's Voice
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Flashback chapter: how Sebastian's radio gift—making strangers feel heard—cost them Nkiru, who said living with Sebastian felt like being a caller, never a partner. Beat: the love story's wound, and the theme of power's cost.

chapters.title: The Choirmaster's Offer
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The entity offers a deal: sing the hymn, keep your voice and your show, and only the dead Okafor line is harvested. Sebastian, exhausted, almost says yes. Nkiru walks in on the negotiation. Beat: temptation at its strongest.

chapters.title: What Love Against Duty Means
chapters.summary: Nkiru's POV. Nkiru argues the pact was never Sebastian's to honor—duty inherited is still a choice. Sebastian counters that refusing means the entity takes the family's dead souls entirely. First real fight, first real honesty in years. Beat: the relationship re-forges under pressure.

chapters.title: The Blank Page Sings
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Holding the page to the mirror, the counter-melody finally appears—but it's written for two voices, and one line is marked: 'to be sung by the one who chooses silence.' Sebastian realizes the cost. Beat: the sacrifice named.

chapters.title: The Dead Ask Too
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The trapped Okafor dead begin calling the house phone—not as the Choirmaster's puppets, but themselves, briefly. Marisol's voice among them. They beg Sebastian not to sing the hymn, and admit they've been its choir for a century. Beat: the dead as victims, not villains.

chapters.title: Adaeze's Confession
chapters.summary: Nkiru's POV via the mirror-writing. Adaeze confesses she wasn't coerced in 1923—she wanted power over audiences and paid willingly, then spent her life trying to warn her descendants. The journal's last line: 'Break it or feed it. There was never a middle.' Beat: the founder's guilt.

chapters.title: House of Hours
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The house begins rearranging itself, rooms folding so the music room is always one door away, the mirrors multiplying. The Choirmaster herds them toward the music room where a piano waits, tuned and patient. Beat: the trap closing.

chapters.title: Nkiru's Choice
chapters.summary: Nkiru's POV. Nkiru realizes she could sing the counter-melody's second voice herself—'a voice given freely to silence' doesn't have to be an Okafor. She tells Sebastian, who refuses to let her pay for his family's sin. Beat: love against duty, both directions.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Sebastian goes to the studio in the house's basement—the transmitter still broadcasting to the entranced city—and addresses the listeners directly, breaking the Choirmaster's hold on the living for one hour by telling the truth on air. Beat: Sebastian's gift turned into a weapon of honesty.

chapters.title: The Choirmaster's True Face
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Furious, the entity stops hiding: it is the accumulated hunger of every voice the family ever silenced—audiences devoured, rivals erased, a century of borrowed belief. It shows Sebastian their own reflection leading its choir. Beat: the horror is inheritance itself.

chapters.title: One Second Behind
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Sebastian realizes the lag isn't a haunting—it's the gap where their stolen voice-shadow lives. If they step into that second, they can take the shadow back. But stepping in means being seen by the Choirmaster directly. Beat: plan formed, price known.

chapters.title: The Step
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Sebastian uncovers every mirror and steps into the lag. Inside the reflected house, they meet their own voice as a separate being—small, starved, singing Adaeze's warning hymn alone for a hundred years. Beat: surreal centerpiece; grief and wonder.

chapters.title: The Choir Breaks
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV, inside the mirror. Sebastian frees their voice-shadow, and the dead Okafors, seeing one of their own refuse the hymn, waver in their rows. The Choirmaster's harmony frays. It screams that it will take the living city instead. Beat: the counterattack begins.

chapters.title: Dawn, Manufactured
chapters.summary: Nkiru's POV. Outside, Nkiru uses the studio transmitter to broadcast the counter-melody's opening bars into the city, waking the entranced listeners, whose collective voices push back the false night. The house's windows begin to lighten. Beat: the siege cracks.

chapters.title: The Final Hymn
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The Choirmaster forces the confrontation in the music room, demanding the hymn at the threshold of real dawn. Sebastian stands at the piano, page in hand, Nkiru beside them, and begins to sing—not the hymn, the counter-melody. Beat: climax opens.

chapters.title: A Voice Given Freely
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Mid-song, the counter-melody demands its price: the singer's voice, surrendered willingly. Nkiru tries to take the line; Sebastian sings it first. The voice leaves them mid-note, and they keep conducting with their hands. Beat: the sacrifice made.

chapters.title: Silence
chapters.summary: Nkiru's POV. The counter-melody completes; the Choirmaster, unharvested and unfed, unravels into a chord that fades. The dead Okafors are released—not saved, but freed. The mirrors sync to real time. Sebastian opens their mouth and nothing comes out. Beat: victory and loss in one breath.

chapters.title: Sunrise, Real This Time
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV, mute. Dawn enters the house for the first time in the book. The tapes in the music room crumble to dust. Sebastian and Nkiru sit on the kitchen floor as the sun climbs, and Sebastian laughs silently until they cry. Beat: exhale after the climax.

chapters.title: The Hour of the Wolf, Final Broadcast
chapters.summary: Nkiru's POV. Nkiru hosts the last episode of Sebastian's show, reading letters from listeners who half-remember being saved by a voice at 3 a.m. Sebastian sits in the studio, silent, smiling, hand on the mixing board. Beat: legacy handed over with grace.

chapters.title: Learning to Listen
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Weeks later: Sebastian teaching themselves to write, to sign, to speak in new ways; Nkiru learning alongside. A new mirror hangs in the hallway, and it reflects exactly on time. Sebastian waves; the reflection waves with them. Beat: quiet healing, theme resolved.

chapters.title: Coda: The Request Line
chapters.summary: Nkiru's POV. Late one night, the station's request line rings once. Nkiru answers. A long pause, then a hummed four notes—not the Choirmaster's, but Sebastian's old show theme. On the couch, mute Sebastian smiles without knowing why. Beat: tender ambiguity, the door closed but not locked.
